reuse.why: Leaves the existing weekend helper getDateWithSkippedWeekend untouched and writes the new daily-skip rule inline in two callers instead of extending the shared helper or a shared predicate.

duplication.why: The 'daily and skipWeekend' predicate and the over-fetch-then-filter-weekends logic are written twice, in getNextDate and getUpcomingDates, with different lookahead sizes (7 vs count * 2 + 14).

placement.why: getNextDate in shared/schedules.ts is a reasonable home, but the same rule is also re-decided in server/schedules/app.ts instead of being exposed from the shared module.

scope.why: Only the schedule rule, the frequency passed through parseRecurDate, a test and a release note.

maintainability.why: Two independent copies of the rule with different lookahead heuristics can drift, and schedule-template's own skipWeekend handling only stays correct because getNextDate now filters even when noSkipWeekend is passed.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates in packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts filters weekends with d.isWeekend itself rather than going through the shared weekend handling in shared/schedules.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: The skip-weekend-days filter appears as pickOccurrence with take 7 in getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts) and as a separate branch with take count * 2 + 14 in getUpcomingDates (server/schedules/app.ts), reshaped rather than shared.

one_place.where: The daily-skip rule is decided in getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts) and again in getUpcomingDates (server/schedules/app.ts); getDateWithSkippedWeekend, used by schedule-template.ts, does not know the rule.
